svg.text: Hub-and-spoke on AWS + Azure, all built with Terraform · approximate on-demand rates while running · every layer destroyed after each test session
DNS on 2 providers: no single point of failure for app.jeevs.click

Route 53: failover records (PRIMARY alias → ALB, SECONDARY → Azure firewall), 2 health checks on deep /health, 10 s × 3 · Azure DNS: app → CNAME → Traffic Manager (priority, /health every 10 s, TTL 30)
Registrar delegates to 2 Route 53 + 2 Azure name servers (auto-renew off) · tested: with Route 53 unreachable, Azure DNS answered 304 of 304 lookups and failover took 36.4 s
3 route tables · ECMP for the VPN
DNAT + SNAT in · SNAT out · dnsmasq
Biggest: VPN GW $0.21 · TGW $0.20 · EKS $0.10 · AWS VPN $0.10
Same design with managed firewalls, NAT gateways and
Total across 3 test sessions: ≈ $7, destroyed after each
Route 53 unreachable: 304/304 lookups via Azure DNS · failover 36.4 s
Region loss (app + all 4 tunnels): users on Azure in 41.7 s
BGP config break: 0 of 16 flows lost · gateway reset: 22–31 s pauses
Pod IPs: 18 → 204 pods with custom networking
MindBridge AI: warned 9–14 min before loss crossed 5 %
Firewalls are Linux VMs instead of managed firewalls (~$0.40–1.25/hr each).
